text.p: Swiss-Swedish engineering group ABB Asea Brown Boveri said it had signed a preliminary agreement with Volvo Car Corporation of Sweden to supply automation equipment.
The agreement is subject to approval by the relevant corporate parties and regulatory authorities.
ABB said it will have a majority shareholding in the new company, which will be part of the existing company ABB Flexible Automation. It will also be responsible for its overall management.
An ABB spokeswoman, elaborating on the statement, said that ABB would have a stake of over 50 stake in the new company but declined to specify the exact amount.
The joint venture will supply equipment for automotive body assembly shops and press lines, ABB said.
It will include Volvo Cars' businesses for assembly line engineering, press automation and lightweight welding guns, which are located in Olofstrom in southern Sweden.
It will also include the operations of Volvo subsidiary Olofstrom Automation, with locations in Toronto, Canada, Detroit, the U.S. and Sao Paulo, ABB said. -- Zurich Editorial, +41 1 631 7340
